paragraphs.text: Teach a DeepSeek Harness agent to reason well, watch its context budget, and hand off long sessions.
Host plugin plus an offline trace analyzer.
# dsh-context-keeper
Two things for a DeepSeek Harness agent:

- **A host plugin** that teaches it how to reason well — one persistent
system-prompt section, visib

le on every request.
- **An offline analyzer** that reads what it actually thought, from the session

uest.
- **An offline analyzer** that reads what it actually thought, from the session
files on disk.

It does **not** cut reasoning short. That was the original goal; measurement
killed it. See Why this
does not reduce thinking.
## Compatibility

- **DeepSeek Harness `>= 0.2.0-rc.1`** — declared in `package.json` under `dsh.engines.dsh`.
- **Nod

e.js `>= 22`** — the plugin uses the built-in `zlib.zstdDecompressSync`.
- **Verified on:** DSH Desk

top **44.7.0** (Windows) — the context badge mounts and
renders in the turn footer, and `/context-wa

tch` / `/handoff` run against local
session files.

The plugin relies on public DSH APIs: `systemPrompt.section`, `commands.register`,
the `conversation

.chat.turnTail` / `conversation.composer.dock` seats, and the
`contextPressure` projection. If a fut

ure build changes those, the host half warns
once and registers nothing instead of taking the host d

own; the client half simply
renders nothing when its projection is unavailable.
## What v0.4 adds: a context badge & reminder

**A colour dot in every turn's footer** (the `conversation.chat.turnTail`
seat — the same place and

shape as dsh-cost-meter's usage chip). It reads the
official `contextPressure` projection and paints

the band — **green (<50%) /
yellow (50–65%) / orange (65–80%) / red (≥80%)** — with the occupancy p

**A reminder panel under the input** (`conversation.composer.dock`) that appears
at **orange/red** o

nly. It states the band and offers an **开新会话** button: it
calls the client Remote `session.create` +

`session.prompt` to make a fresh
session in the same workspace and seed it with "read the latest ha

ndoff package
under `.context-keeper/handoff` and continue". The new session is a full agent,
so it

reads the package itself — the button does not inline the package (that
would spend tokens again).

Both are pure presentation plus one explicit user click. They never enter the
model input on their o
wn and cost zero tokens until you press the button.

> **Honest limits** (verified against this build's source):
> - DSH's `ReasoningRow` header (above t

he thinking block) is hard-wired with no
>   extension seat, so the footer is the nearest always-vis

ible open spot.
> - After creating the new session the button **cannot switch you to it** — the
>

slot API has no navigation; open it from the sidebar. The panel says so.
> - Command **names** must

match `^[a-z][a-z0-9_-]*$` and third-party commands
>   render their name (no separate display `labe

l`), so `/handoff` and
>   `/context-watch` cannot be shown as `Handoff`/`Context-Watch` in the menu

.
>   Readability goes into the **Chinese one-line description** shown next to
>   each name instead

>   Readability goes into the **Chinese one-line description** shown next to
>   each name instead.

The client half is `plugin/client.js` (declared under `dsh.client` in
`package.json`); the host half
is unchanged. No config path needed.
## What v0.3 adds: context budget & handoff

v0.2 taught the agent *how* to think. v0.3 handles *whether the window can hold
it*. Two human comma

nds, both reading the session file DSH already writes and
calling a model **zero times**:

- **`/context-watch`** — occupancy, band (green/yellow/orange/red), headroom,
growth per turn, and t

he last compaction's reclaim.
- **`/handoff`** — write a portable handoff package plus a full faithf

ul archive
to `<workspace>/.context-keeper/handoff/`, so a fresh session can continue
without re-der

iving anything. It reuses DSH's own `compaction/summary`
checkpoint as the "early context" (free mul

ti-level distillation) and quotes
the recent tail verbatim.

A short, **static** context-budget line is added to the system prompt. It holds
no numbers on purpos

e: a changing number in the system prompt would invalidate
the provider's prefix cache on every requ
est, which costs more than it saves.

The design and the two references it distils are in
docs/distill-design-v3.md.
## The plugin: what it puts in the prompt

The rule is five lines, each naming an observable behaviour rather than a
virtue:

> **Decide before acting.** Before the first tool call, settle what you are
> doing, why, and how yo

u will know it worked. Once you state a plan, execute
> it; do not reopen the plan mid-execution.
>

> **Change a conclusion only with a reason.** …
>
> **When reasoning stalls, gather evidence instead

of thinking harder.** …
>
> **Match depth to risk.** Read-only exploration may be quick. Irreversib

le
> actions deserve a second look. …
>
> **Say what you do not know.** …

Full text and the reasoning behind each line: plugin/rule.mjs
and docs/rule-text.md.
### Why a prompt section and not a stream interceptor

The first design watched the reasoning stream and reacted — lower the effort
tier when a trace looke

d wasteful, stop a turn that ran away. Three
measurements, on real sessions, removed the target:
| Hypothesis | Measured | Result |

| Looping traces repeat sentences | 0.1% sentence repetition | dead |
| Nearby steps re-derive earli

er steps | 0.3% of step pairs above Jaccard 0.35 | dead |
| Early commitment + long tail = waste | t
op candidates read by hand: both productive | dead |

It also depended on two fragile places: `llm/stream` (no in-tree consumer) and
`agent/turn-stopping`
(fires only after the turn already ended).

A prompt section is the opposite kind of intervention. It is declared once, it
is visible on every r

equest, and it needs no detection — the model does not have
to be caught in a bad pattern in order t

o learn from it. Numbers and raw data:
docs/calibration.md.
## The CLI: reading what it thought

| Metric | Meaning |

| `tokens` | Estimated thinking tokens |
| `paras` | Paragraphs in the trace |
| `commit@` | Where t

he first commitment to a plan lands, as a share of the trace |
